name: Drowned Sacellum
summary: At Blackfathom Deeps' entrance, the Drowned Sacellum lies beneath the coast. Murlocs and makrura now haunt its broken stones amid brackish pools and cavern roots.

sections.title: A Submerged Sanctuary
sections.body: You pass Blackfathom Deeps' threshold into the Drowned Sacellum. Once a quiet place of worship to Elune, the chapel has long lain collapsed beneath Ashenvale's coast. Brackish pools cover its ancient marble flagstones. Starfish cling beneath great roots in the cavern ceiling, while dark wisps flicker through the gloom. Follow the broken stone path with care, and it leads deeper into the temple complex toward the Pool of Ask'ar.

sections.title: Den of Scavengers
sections.body: Night elf caretakers left the Drowned Sacellum long ago. Now shoreline scavengers hold the ruins. Aggressive murlocs and heavily armored makrura share the murky waters, attacking anyone who disturbs their nesting grounds. Darker cultic threats lie deeper in the temple. These predators guard the first stretch of the underground ruins.

faq.q: What was the Drowned Sacellum originally used for?
faq.answer: Before the Sundering, the Drowned Sacellum was an elven place of worship to Elune. It stood within the greater underground temple complex.

faq.q: What creatures inhabit this part of the caverns?
faq.answer: Wild murlocs and makrura inhabit the flooded ruins. They thrive in brackish pools and nesting crevices.

faq.q: How do you navigate past the Drowned Sacellum?
aliases: how to get through drowned sacellum
faq.answer: Cross the crumbling platforms and pillars that rise half-submerged from the water. The tunnel ahead leads to the Pool of Ask'ar.

faq.q: Where does the light in the cavern come from?
faq.answer: Dark wisps drift among thick, twisted roots that pierce the cavern ceiling from the Ashenvale forests above. They cast the cavern's faint, eerie light.

angles.text: As a night elf, you see an ancient shrine submerged in saltwater and occupied by murlocs. It recalls the Kaldorei heritage lost beneath the Zoram Strand.
As a druid, you can see massive tree roots piercing the stone ceiling from the surface above. Nature endures amid the corrupted underground waters.
